design:
Part of the htgr_sim_v1 execution-architecture epic (bn op-276r). Design reference: `docs/architecture/htgr-sim-execution.md`.


Specify the message protocol before building the pool.

Constraints:

- messages carry a **timestep id** so late results are discarded rather than
  applied out of order
- transferable payloads where practical; avoid copying large arrays
- a worker is **stateless between dispatches**, or its state is explicitly
  owned and versioned — **hidden worker state breaks determinism**
- results reconciled only when **every** kernel in the timestep has reported;
  partial reconciliation is never published
- **expressible without `SharedArrayBuffer`**

That last constraint is load-bearing: shared memory needs COOP/COEP headers
that **GitHub Pages does not serve**, so requiring it would forfeit the static
hosting goal.

**Acceptance:** a written protocol spec plus Rust types, with a round-trip test.


**Branch:** `develop` only. Do not merge or push to `main`.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content: Protocol must be generic across simulators, not HTGR-shaped (2026-09-06 decision: pool is unconditional and must carry a refinery flowsheet as its second consumer). Concretely: no fixed kernel count, no assumption that every kernel runs every timestep, no HTGR subsystem names in the protocol types.

title: HTGR exec: Worker protocol and data-transfer types

description: The thermal pincell (op-6tz.12) is LIVE at k_inf=1.39802+/-0.00652 but only verified (physical band), not validated. Run HIGH-tier (net-fetch from_endf) U235/238/O16 + real OpenMC pincell with same materials/geometry and compare k_inf. See REVIEW_MANIFEST op-6tz-thermal-pincell.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
Code-to-code comparison DONE (2026-07-15) vs openmc pincell.ipynb stored output (openmc-notebooks @ cf1e5db, MIT). SAME spec confirmed: 3% UO2 @10.0 g/cc, fuel r=0.39 / clad 0.46 cm, pitch 1.26 cm, Zr clad, water + c_H_in_H2O, reflective BC, 293.6 K.
  RESULT: outram-mc k_inf = 1.39802 ± 0.00652  vs  OpenMC 1.40544 ± 0.00302.
  Δk = -742 pcm (-0.531%); combined σ = 0.00719 → agree within 1.03σ (statistically consistent).
  CAVEATS (why this is a cross-check, not a validation): (a) different data — ours = CORE WMP (ENDF/B-VII.1) + free-gas + tsl-HinH2O (ENDF/B-VIII.0); notebook = NNDC HDF5 pointwise CE; library differences alone routinely ~100s pcm. (b) our σ is 2x larger (600 part x 60 active vs 1000 x 90). (c) WMP+free-gas resonance treatment vs pointwise CE — U-238 capture fidelity differs.
  Not closed: a same-data, higher-statistics run (and ideally an actual OpenMC run on identical XS) would make this a true validation. Left open for that.

title: outram-mc: benchmark-validate thermal UO2 pincell k_inf vs real OpenMC

description:
`petir::real::{exp, ln, powf}` now default to PETIR's ports of ARM
optimized-routines (commit 663124c04), and `outram-mc-libs` reaches them
through its `RealMath` trait. **The other four PETIR consumers do not** —
they still call `f64::exp` / `f64::ln` / `f64::powf` directly, i.e. the
platform libm, so their results are still platform-dependent in the last ulp.

Direct f64 transcendental call sites, counted 2026-09-14
(`grep -rn "\.exp()\|\.ln()\|\.powf(" crates/<c>/src --include=*.rs`):

| crate | sites |
|---|---|
| outram-park-fork-coolprop | 288 |
| njoy-outram-park-fork | 211 |
| tampines-steam-tables | 173 |
| outram-foam-basic-lib | 115 |

## Why this is now worth doing, when it was not before

`op-chyp.5` made the PETIR route opt-in because it was a musl-derived `libm`
route and `libm` is slower than the platform (1.74x on exp, 1.43x on ln).
That argument is gone for these three functions. Measured from Rust over
2 000 000 calls per route, five runs:

    exp    1.75-1.86x faster than the old libm route; 0.70-0.75x of platform
    ln     1.09-1.18x faster;                         1.04-1.25x of platform
    powf   2.09-2.18x faster;                         1.41-1.57x of platform

`exp` is FASTER than the platform (it inlines instead of calling through a
dynamic symbol). So for `exp` and `ln` this is close to free, and `powf` is
the only one that costs.

## What to do

Reuse `outram-mc-libs::mathf`'s shape rather than inventing a second one —
the `r_`-prefixed trait exists precisely so a sweep is a mechanical rename,
not an expression rewrite. Consider lifting `RealMath` into PETIR itself so
all five crates share one trait instead of copying it four times.

## What to check before claiming it done

**The bits move.** ARM's exp and musl's and glibc's are three different
implementations. Each crate's suite must be re-run and any full-`f64`-
precision fixture re-baselined once, with the move recorded — the same
discipline `op-chyp.6` used. `tampines-steam-tables` is IF97-verified to
1e-8, far looser than 1 ulp, so it should be unaffected; `njoy-outram-park-fork`
agrees with NJOY2016 to 7 significant figures, likewise. Check rather than
assume.

Note `cargo test -p tampines-steam-tables` currently fails in this
environment for an unrelated reason: its egui/eframe 0.36.1 dev-dependencies
require rustc 1.95 and the toolchain here is 1.94.1. The library itself
builds and that failure predates this work.

description:
THE MOST VALUABLE FINDING OF THE WASM AUDIT. This is a genuine latent bug, not a build-config issue, and it would bite any 32-bit target — not just wasm.

  crates/outram-park-mpi/src/communicator.rs:53
    pub(crate) const COLL_CONTEXT_OFFSET: usize = 1 << 40;
  error[E0080]: attempt to shift left by 40_i32, which would overflow

wasm32 has a 32-BIT usize, so '1 << 40' as usize is a compile-time overflow. outram-park-fork-pflotran fails the same way (2 errors).

The code silently assumes 64-bit usize. On a 64-bit host it works; on wasm32 (and on armv7-linux-androideabi and i686-linux-android — both of which the Android rule nominally covers!) it does not. Worth checking whether the armv7/i686 Android targets were ever actually built, because this would have failed there too.

Fix is not merely 'make it compile': decide what the constant MEANS. If it is a tag/offset needing 40 bits of range, it must be u64 and the surrounding arithmetic must be u64, not usize. Widening the type is correct; truncating the constant to fit 32 bits would silently change behaviour and is the wrong fix.

Audit both crates for other width assumptions while in there — grep for 'as usize', '1 <<', and size_of::<usize>().

Acceptance: both pass the wasm --lib check; the constant's semantics are preserved and documented; add a test pinning the intended range.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
Fixed. Both crates now pass cargo check --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown.

Root cause was as suspected — a genuine 64-bit usize assumption, not a build-config issue:
  crates/outram-park-mpi/src/communicator.rs:53
    pub(crate) const COLL_CONTEXT_OFFSET: usize = 1 << 40;
wasm32 has a 32-bit usize, so this was a compile-time overflow.

Fix: WIDENED the communicator context id to u64 throughout rather than truncating the constant, because the value is a numeric namespace tag and not a memory size — truncating to fit 32 bits would have silently collapsed the 40-bit separation the collective/point-to-point isolation argument depends on. Sites changed: WORLD_COMM_ID, COLL_CONTEXT_OFFSET, Communicator::comm_id field + accessor, coll_ctx(), alloc_context(), send_ctx/recv_ctx ctx params, Envelope::comm_id, Transport::next_comm_id (AtomicUsize -> AtomicU64), alloc_comm_id(), agree_new_context(), the split() context-map decode, and the transport test helper. A doc block on the constant now records why it is u64.

outram-park-fork-pflotran needed NO separate fix — its 2 errors were the same constant reached through its outram-park-mpi dependency, and it went green as soon as mpi did.

Verification: cargo check --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown 0 errors for both; cargo check --all-targets native 0 errors; cargo test --release -p outram-park-mpi 35 passed.

WIDER FINDING worth acting on separately: this would equally have failed on armv7-linux-androideabi and i686-linux-android, which the workspace Android rule nominally covers. That strongly suggests the 32-bit Android targets have never actually been built — the rule's acceptance command names aarch64 only. Worth a bead against epic op-zfr.

title: wasm class E: 64-bit usize assumptions — real portability bug (pflotran, outram-park-mpi)
